basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Pluit Dominus ignem et sulphur de coelo. Ignis ardorem habet, sulphur fetorem.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Pluit Dominus ignem et sulphur de coelo. Ignis ardorem habet, sulphur fetorem. Quia ergo isti flamma libidinis arserant et in fetore carnis versabantur, juste simul igne et sulphure perierunt. Considerandum hoc loco quod primos peccatores aqua diluvii exterminavit, quia et ipsi similiter carnis concupiscentia Deum offenderant. Sodomitae vero graviori supplicio, id est: ignis et sulphuris diluvio perierunt, quia illi, licet mensuram excederent, naturaliter tamen peccabant cum feminis, isti vero, irrationabiliter et contra naturam, ideo gravissimo supplicii exemplo damnati sunt.
